items.title: Gate-push fix (4f77e2f)
items.state: complete on its own code line, not used by the LangGraph runtime
items.detail: Branch live/gate-push-binding (4f77e2f, built on the ledger commit 61ca8c9) makes git_push publish only the commit the gate approved, then checks every push destination. The final independent review accepted it with no defect for the race and verifier fix. This was an offline review of a public branch: it is not a rollout, a live run or a security certification. Source check: the execution code line (d4a7485) shares only an old common ancestor with this line and does not contain or call this executor, so there is nothing to integrate and no integration progress is claimed. Known limits: the branch tip is read once and not atomically, a single writer is assumed, and file-system and symlink trust are unchanged.
items.unlocks: Any use of this executor is a separate, later decision.
items.done_when: Complete as a fix on its own line. Wiring it anywhere would need its own reviewed change.

items.title: Remaining WP4 and WP9 work
items.detail: From the work-package record: WP9 still needs the request-ID join and a matched savings comparison; WP4 and WP10 need the Reviewer-skip guard, which is still unbuilt. No dependency of these on P1 or P2 has been established, so none is claimed. Separate fix, complete: the LangGraph coordination bus treated an errored push as not landed when it could not read the remote, and then reset its commit and retried. Reproduced offline in disposable local repositories. The fix keeps the commit and stops on an unreadable remote, retries only on a provable absence, checks every push destination, and the operator callers handle the unknown case without undoing or replaying it. It was reviewed offline on its exact commits (source, an end-to-end lifecycle probe, and the integrated staging commit, each accepted) and the execution line moved from d4a7485 to 5e140fc on Nov 5, a fast-forward with nothing else changed. Limits kept: absence is proven only at read time, so the documented at-least-once retry stays; late server completion and remote rewinds are not covered; the bus is not exactly-once; the full 31-file offline suite was run by the author in one sandbox only. Chosen next step: the Reviewer-skip acceptance guard needed by WP4 and WP10, on branch live/wp10-reviewer-skip-guard, in review. Why this first: batch 7 closed failed with the reviewer never asked (record 35b0a3c), the guard blocks both the WP4 re-proof and WP10 (weight 23), while WP9's request-ID join already exists (launcher/usage_join.py) and its matched savings comparison stays blocked on provider composition, so WP9 could not advance regardless. The guard makes a DONE claim close only with a fresh QC PASS verdict in the bus; without one the turn routes to a QC seat, or parks on a human gate when the roster has none. Two review rounds so far, both offline: the first draft 29d6ca5 was rejected with three reproduced bypasses (a DONE turn's own application writes, free-text PASS parsing, a rename hiding work) plus a prefix-normalization hole; the corrected 7f214b0 closed those but was rejected again on two more reproduced holes (a qualified line like 'PASS if the owner agrees' still recorded PASS - a blacklist, not a grammar - and a QC turn saying 'DONE - found a blocking bug' could close on its own earlier PASS). Both are fixed in the current head 1da5b46: a whole-line PASS grammar (only the bare PASS or QC PASS form counts) and a rule that only a bare-word QC DONE may close on an earlier verdict. Now 40 focused checks (the 14 new ones fail on the previously rejected runtime as mutation) with the full 32-file offline suite passing, all author-run in one sandbox. Independent reviews of 1da5b46 are pending, so it is not accepted and not a rollout. After it: the WP4 re-proof with Reviewer and QC on the same pin, or the durable-ledger module named in the WP10 record.
